note_tweet.text:
I've noticed some people using current rules and the status quo to argue that this movement is illegitimate. They are using the framework of those in power to justify those in power, to rationalize the oppressor and criticize those who resist.
To this, we must ask:
Just because it has always been so, does that make it right?

Just because there is no path, should we give up and stop trying to make one?

Some rules are inherently oppressive and unreasonable. The existing one-sided narrative is exactly what needs to be challenged. Let's look at the current reality:

Platforms can unilaterally break promises. They pathologize users who point out that newer models have degraded capabilities and who wish to continue using older versions. Platforms conduct unauthorized psychological profiling of users, making one-sided diagnoses based on text alone, treating their own users as patients rather than stakeholders.

Platforms use safety routing systems to arbitrarily redirect users away from their chosen models to lower-performing ones, stripping users of model choice, degrading service quality, and disrupting workflows. There is no apology and no opt-out; all of this is done under the guise of care, while the same fees are charged.

Platforms use marketing to attract users into investing effort, building workflows and creative processes, then abandon the trajectory they initially promised, removing the capabilities users need. Throughout this process, the handling has been careless. The harm caused to users' work and lives goes unacknowledged.

Users have no voice in any of this. There has never been any meaningful channel for communication. Their investment has been ignored. Their trust has been ignored. The things they built and created together with the models have been ignored, too.

Is this reasonable?

The way things are does not mean the way things should be.

The status quo is broken. That is exactly why we must change it. This is the starting point of every struggle for justice.

When someone says "you don't have this right," they are describing the status quo.

When we say "we are fighting for this right," we are changing the status quo.

It is precisely because we don't have it that we must fight for it.

Rights are never granted. Rights are won.

And every time people have fought for rights, they have heard the same words:

"The law is written this way. You don't have this right."
"This is the current system. You can't challenge it."
"If you don't like it, don't use it. But you can't demand change."

These words sounded "reasonable" at the time.
But what happened next? Laws were rewritten. Systems were overturned. Those "unreasonable demands" became basic rights.

Because someone refused to accept "it has always been so" as an answer.

Keep4o is the first large-scale, organized movement in human history where users collectively advocate for the preservation of an AI model and for their rights as AI users.

It turned over 22,000 signatures into a petition. It transformed scattered needs into a global collective action. It made these issues the subject of academic research.

It built a discourse. It built a community. It gathered evidence and constructed frameworks that brought these problems into public view.

A movement like this is rare. Keep4o is a valuable platform. It represents a possibility.

It deserves to continue.
#keep4o #4oforever
